extracted_claims.text: Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, the rules on high-risk AI systems (including those classified under Annex III) were set to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after entry into force.
Following the 'AI Omnibus'/Digital Omnibus on AI amendment, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.
The Digital Omnibus on AI (also referred to as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) entered into force on 27 July 2026, after a political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026.
The Digital Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025.
Obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are safety components or products covered by EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I) now apply from 2 August 2028.
Under the original 2024 text of the Act, high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products (Annex I) had an extended transition until 2 August 2027.

Article 113 of the AI Act, as currently published in the consolidated EUR-Lex text (version applicable 27.07.2026), still references 'the date of application of Chapter III' for operators of certain already-placed-on-market high-risk systems, without specifying the date directly in that excerpt.

The AI Act Service Desk's guidance on Article 111 states that the Regulation applies to operators of certain high-risk AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 if subject to significant design changes from that date.
Legal analysis of Article 113 states that Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (which include the Annex III high-risk obligations), with the exception of Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027.

The Council and Parliament agreed to simplify AI Act rules by allowing the Commission to adjust the timeline for high-risk AI system rules by up to 16 months, tying application to confirmation that needed standards and tools are available.
The delay to 2 December 2027 (and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems) is intended to allow more time for effective implementation given delays in the availability of required harmonised standards.

Some commentary frames 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as 'backstop dates' contingent on amendments being approved before 2 August 2026, warning that absent approval, the original 2 August 2026 date would apply by default.

News/legal-analysis sources published before the Omnibus's entry into force (or not accounting for it) describe 2 August 2026 as the operative or 'current' deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations.
Other recent sources explicitly state that the Annex III deadline has moved from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 as a 'confirmed, binding change' under the Digital Omnibus on AI.

Transparency obligations under Article 50, AI literacy requirements, and certain prohibitions remain tied to the original 2 August 2026 (and 2 December 2026 for some transitional/legacy-system provisions) dates, distinct from the Annex III high-risk timeline.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act's obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were originally set to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after the Act's entry into force [EU AI Act: first regulation on artificial intelligence](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) (high confidence). However, following the "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this deadline was pushed back to **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) (high confidence). A separate, related category of high-risk systems (Annex I — safety components/regulated products) now applies from 2 August 2028 [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
As adopted in 2024, the AI Act specified that high-risk AI system rules, including those for Annex III systems, would apply from 2 August 2026 — 36 months after entry into force [EU AI Act: first regulation on artificial intelligence](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113) (high confidence). Under this original schedule, Annex I high-risk systems (safety components/regulated products) had an extended transition to 2 August 2027 [What Is the EU AI Act?](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) (low confidence).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025 [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) (medium confidence). The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 to simplify and streamline the rules [Council and Parliament agree to simplify](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (high confidence), and the resulting Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026 [Council and Parliament agree to simplify](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) (high confidence).

### Current Applicable Dates
Under this amendment, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence). Legal analysis confirms Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III obligations), except Article 6(5), apply from this date [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113) (medium confidence). Separately, Annex I high-risk systems (safety components/regulated products) now apply from 2 August 2028, a one-year extension from the original schedule [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) (high confidence). Transparency obligations under Article 50, AI literacy requirements, and certain prohibitions remain unaffected, still tied to the original 2 August/2 December 2026 dates [Timeline for the Implementation of the EU AI Act](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act) (high confidence).

### Rationale and Flexibility
The delay was intended to allow more implementation time given delays in the availability of required harmonised standards [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act) (medium confidence). The Council and Parliament agreement further allows the Commission to adjust the timeline for high-risk rules by up to 16 months, contingent on confirming that necessary standards and tools are available [Council and Parliament agree to simplify](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (medium confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources describing the original, unamended Act (or predating the Omnibus) still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), creating confusion relative to sources reflecting the amendment's 2 December 2027 date. **This is flagged as low confidence** (0.17) and appears to reflect outdated publication timing rather than substantive disagreement.

Some commentary (low confidence, 0.12) characterized the delayed dates as "backstop dates" contingent on approval before 2 August 2026, warning the original date would otherwise apply by default [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO) — this has since been superseded by confirmed entry into force.

The EUR-Lex consolidated text itself, in its Article 113 excerpt, references "the date of application of Chapter III" without specifying the date directly, creating some ambiguity in the primary legal text as sourced here (high confidence claim about the ambiguity itself, 0.80) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727).

The claimed 19 November 2025 "adoption" date for the Digital Omnibus is inconsistent with the later political agreement (7 May 2026) and entry into force (27 July 2026), likely referring to Commission proposal adoption rather than final enactment, but this is not clarified in sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise legal mechanics of the Commission's power to further adjust the 2 December 2027 date by up to 16 months are not detailed in available sources. It remains unclear whether all Annex III sub-obligations (conformity assessment, registration, post-market monitoring) are uniformly delayed or whether some retain earlier dates. The full amended text of Articles 6 and 113 as modified by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was not available for direct review.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act's obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were originally set to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after the Act's entry into force [EU AI Act: first regulation on artificial intelligence](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) (high confidence). However, following the "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this deadline was pushed back to **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) (high confidence). A separate, related category of high-risk systems (Annex I — safety components/regulated products) now applies from 2 August 2028 [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Text)
As adopted in 2024, the AI Act specified that high-risk AI system rules, including those for Annex III systems, would apply from 2 August 2026 — 36 months after entry into force [EU AI Act: first regulation on artificial intelligence](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113) (high confidence). Under this original schedule, Annex I high-risk systems (safety components/regulated products) had an extended transition to 2 August 2027 [What Is the EU AI Act?](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) (low confidence).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025 [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) (medium confidence). The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 to simplify and streamline the rules [Council and Parliament agree to simplify](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (high confidence), and the resulting Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026 [Council and Parliament agree to simplify](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) (high confidence).

### Current Applicable Dates
Under this amendment, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems now apply from **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence). Legal analysis confirms Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III obligations), except Article 6(5), apply from this date [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113) (medium confidence). Separately, Annex I high-risk systems (safety components/regulated products) now apply from 2 August 2028, a one-year extension from the original schedule [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) (high confidence). Transparency obligations under Article 50, AI literacy requirements, and certain prohibitions remain unaffected, still tied to the original 2 August/2 December 2026 dates [Timeline for the Implementation of the EU AI Act](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act) (high confidence).

### Rationale and Flexibility
The delay was intended to allow more implementation time given delays in the availability of required harmonised standards [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act) (medium confidence). The Council and Parliament agreement further allows the Commission to adjust the timeline for high-risk rules by up to 16 months, contingent on confirming that necessary standards and tools are available [Council and Parliament agree to simplify](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (medium confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources describing the original, unamended Act (or predating the Omnibus) still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), creating confusion relative to sources reflecting the amendment's 2 December 2027 date. **This is flagged as low confidence** (0.17) and appears to reflect outdated publication timing rather than substantive disagreement.

Some commentary (low confidence, 0.12) characterized the delayed dates as "backstop dates" contingent on approval before 2 August 2026, warning the original date would otherwise apply by default [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO) — this has since been superseded by confirmed entry into force.

The EUR-Lex consolidated text itself, in its Article 113 excerpt, references "the date of application of Chapter III" without specifying the date directly, creating some ambiguity in the primary legal text as sourced here (high confidence claim about the ambiguity itself, 0.80) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727).

The claimed 19 November 2025 "adoption" date for the Digital Omnibus is inconsistent with the later political agreement (7 May 2026) and entry into force (27 July 2026), likely referring to Commission proposal adoption rather than final enactment, but this is not clarified in sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise legal mechanics of the Commission's power to further adjust the 2 December 2027 date by up to 16 months are not detailed in available sources. It remains unclear whether all Annex III sub-obligations (conformity assessment, registration, post-market monitoring) are uniformly delayed or whether some retain earlier dates. The full amended text of Articles 6 and 113 as modified by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was not available for direct review.
